title: Increasing-cutoff stress for the conditional birth-death gap
question: Does the conditional birth-death spectral gap used by R-399 remain bounded away from zero when the Q3 oscillator cutoff is increased, or does the high-level tail create a route-local bottleneck?

new_perspective.principle: Stress the conditional reference geometry before spending effort on real-time gradients.
route: Use the exact finite Q3 Gibbs coordinate law as the reference measure and compute every oriented-prefix conditional law, without a source-history sample that could mask a reference bottleneck.
For each conditional law, form the reversible ordered-level birth-death Laplacian with conductance min(pi(k),pi(k+1)) and extract the first nonzero generalized gap.
Repeat beta in {1/2,1,2}, volume two through three and cutoffs through eight where the exact dense diagonalisation remains feasible.

Retain per-cutoff minima, adjacent ratios and smallest conditional atom. A positive low-cutoff minimum is not extrapolated; a systematic collapse is a route-specific obstruction to this Dirichlet choice.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A cutoff-stable conditional gap would be one input to the R-399 shell-gradient route. This static Gibbs stress does not provide likelihood-gradient decay, common-core control, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or a physical gap.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity of finite gap ratios and minima; it does not formalize Q3 spectra or any cutoff limit.

promotion_criteria: Extend the static gap computation to a phase-conditioned boundary family and prove a cutoff-, volume- and shape-uniform lower bound for a physically justified local form.
Only if that lower bound survives, prove uniform decay of the R-399 conditional likelihood gradients and sum the weighted shell transfer.
stop_conditions: If the minimum conditional gap tends to zero under an increasing-cutoff stress, retain R-399 as a finite interface and mark this birth-death route locally obstructed for uniform promotion.
If the static gap remains positive but adjacent ratios oscillate without a certified modulus, do not infer a limit; move to an analytic conditional-measure estimate.
If the gap is stable only at finite beta, restrict the route to fixed-beta statements and keep the ground/phase gate open.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite static cutoff stress. It proves no uniform conditional gap, gradient decay, common form core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: A finite positive gap and a finite cutoff profile are diagnostics. Neither is a thermodynamic lower bound or a Q3 real-time locality theorem.
